tells.1: Forced casualness ('and honestly, that's the fun part', 'your opinion will actually count') plus tidy bold labels on every section
tells.2: Slightly over-smoothed rhythm, with the stock triad 'real days off, nights that actually end, and a schedule you can plan a life around'
tells.3: Mild template polish ('keeping standards high without turning the kitchen into a pressure cooker'), but otherwise plain and natural
tells.4: Same 'pressure cooker' flourish and triad; little else stands out
tells.5: none (all caps, run-on punctuation and typos read as an unskilled human, not AI)
tells.6: Neat bold-label scaffolding ('What you'll do:', 'What we're after:') with en/em dashes, which gives it a templated feel

reason: Version 4 is clear, warm and specific without looking formatted for a template or straining to sound casual. Version 5 is obviously human but unprofessional, and Version 1 overcorrects with inserted conversational filler.
